title: Paul Norez and his barbecue place sessions
summary: Russell describes visiting trumpeter Paul Norez at his barbecue place, with Monday-night sessions, and his short notes on him.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah, it's surprising. A couple more generations, they'll be faded out completely. Yeah. Another interview I have here, which is these longhand things are in pitiful shape as far as being word for word, is Paul Norez. I used to go to see him when he had a little barbecue place up on North State Street, about 800 block. Specialized in a secret formulae claimed of barbecue sauce. He was probably a pretty good cook though, and still a good trumpet player. Had sessions there on Monday nights of all the New Orleans musicians, whoever was there, like the Bob Crosby band, say if Zola or Johnny Dodds, he'd have Johnny and Baby come in quite often. Had some very good sessions. I only heard maybe one or two, I don't know if I heard more than one that I can say for sure, but he wasn't a great talker, but he still knew a lot of the fellows and had a lot to say on New Orleans music. I have only a page and a half of his here too.
